Feed that remainder with equal parts flour and water by weight (start smaller, like 20g starter to 20g flour and 20g water) and leave it at room temperature, not the fridge. Expect it to look sluggish or barely rise for the first 1 to 2 feedings — that's expected recovery, not failure. Feed it again every 12 to 24 hours for 3 to 5 days; you're looking for it to double in size within 6 to 8 hours of a feeding before you trust it for baking. blunt_right: Add a running-balance column and a runway column. If your columns are B=Month, C=Income, D=Fixed Costs, E=Variable Costs, and your current cash is in a labeled cell like H1: in F2 put =H1+C2-D2-E2 for the first row, then in F3 put =F2+C3-D3-E3 and fill down — that gives running balance per month. For a single months-of-runway number instead of a row-by-row balance, use =H1/((AVERAGE(D2:D13)+AVERAGE(E2:E13))-AVERAGE(C2:C13)); if income is zero or near-zero right now, simplify to =H1/AVERAGE(D2:D13,E2:E13), which is current cash divided by average monthly burn. If you want it to fail gracefully while the sheet is still empty, wrap it: =IFERROR(H1/(AVERAGE(D2:D13)+AVERAGE(E2:E13)-AVERAGE(C2:C13)),"N/A"). Put your current cash balance in a clearly labeled single cell, not buried in a row, so the formula references it cleanly. Since you specifically asked about rent: add one more column isolating rent from other fixed costs, then use =H1/RENT_CELL for a simple months-of-rent-covered number. Go to bed once this is in — the formula will still be there at a reasonable hour.

blunt_right: Question set, same six each month for trend tracking: 1) On a scale of 1-5, how manageable has your workload been this month? 2) Have you worked unpaid overtime in the last four weeks — how often? 3) Do you feel you can raise a concern with me without it affecting how you're treated? 4) Is anything happening outside work affecting how you're coping? 5) What's one thing that would make your job easier right now? 6) Any changes since last month I should know about? Log template, one row per session: date, staff name, manager, numeric scores for Q1-Q2, free-text notes on Q3-Q6, action agreed (if any), follow-up date, escalated to HR (Y/N). That will likely eat most or all of the $9,000 before you've sold a single crêpe. Don't drop the part-time job yet. A chart where most children never move and a small minority repeatedly land on public sanction isn't evidence of behaviour change — it's evidence of who's easiest to sort. Research on public clip/colour charts links them to increased shame and anxiety, disproportionate targeting of children with ADHD, trauma histories or SEND, and no lasting change in the behaviour they flag. The calm you're seeing may reflect compliance from fear rather than the outcome you want written up as pedagogy.
